Hi Alex — great question, and glad the demo was helpful. I put together a short overview and a high-level transfer diagram (attached) that answers the specific bullets below. Short answers up front:

- Regions: Primary execution occurs in the region you select (we currently support US, EU, APAC regions). Routing defaults to the region tied to your account but can be pinned per-model or per-route.
- Subprocessors: Core compute runs on our managed clusters (we use AWS/GCP in-region), and we use third-party monitoring/metrics providers for telemetry (list attached).
- Transient processing: We perform ephemeral cross-region fallbacks for availability in rare cases; we document all fallback paths and keep KV caches region-local where possible.
- Retention/deletion: Short-term logs/metrics are retained for 30 days by default; model request/response data retention is configurable — standard deletion requests trigger a 72-hour purge from active storage and a 90-day deletion from backups and logs (we provide certs/evidence on request).

See the attached: data-processing-overview.pdf (one-pager) and a brief subprocessor CSV listing. If your team needs a formal transfer map image or signed attestation for procurement, I can loop in our infra/security engineer.

Next step: do you want me to introduce Dev to go through the transfer map with your engineering/security folks?

Best,

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Hi all — thanks for the ping, Alex. Below is a concise, technical answer you can share with your security team. I included a simple ASCII transfer map and noted where ephemeral processing can occur. Attaching a PNG of the transfer map and the latest subprocessor CSV.

Short technical summary:
- Primary execution region: Requests are routed to the customer-selected region (US region = us-east-1 / us-west-2 by default). Requests originating in the US are served in-region unless capacity/failover policy triggers an alternate execution zone.
- Subprocessors that may see request or metadata (examples):
  * Compute: AWS EC2 (Redwood-managed instances in selected region)
  * Model caching/kv-store: Redis clusters managed by Redwood (hosted on GCP or AWS depending on region)
  * Observability/metrics: Datadog (metrics/alerts only), Sentry (error traces can contain truncated request IDs but not full payloads)
  * Storage/backups: GCS or S3 buckets (encrypted at rest); backups are geo-redundant per customer retention policy
- Cross-border/transient processing:
  * Sojourns: For high-availability fallbacks, we may route a small percentage of requests to a failover region (e.g., EU) for execution. These paths are rare (occurs under capacity pressure or regional outage) and are logged.
  * Caching: Prefix and KV caches are strongly preferred to remain in-region; however, cache warmups may pull small artifacts across regions during initialization for performance.
- Data in transit and at rest:
  * All request payloads and responses are encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest (AES-256). Keys are managed via customer KMS where configured.
- Retention and deletion:
  * Active storage purge: 72 hours to remove primary copies after a deletion request (configurable for enterprise customers).
  * Backups/logs: Up to 90 days for backups and derived logs; we can shorten this for contractual agreements.
  * Audit trail: We keep an immutable audit trail of the deletion operation (admin id, timestamp) for 365 days. The trail does not contain full payloads.

Simple transfer map (logical):
  Customer App -> Regional Ingress (load balancer, in-region) -> In-region Redwood Runtime (compute, KV cache) -> Optional Telemetry (Datadog/Sentry) -> Regional Object Storage (backups)
  Fallback path (rare): Regional Ingress -> Alternate Region Runtime (if failover triggered)

Evidence and artifacts we can provide:
- Transfer map image (attached: transfer_map_v1.png)
- Full subprocessor inventory with contact & SOC evidence references (attached CSV)
- Deletion attestation PDF (we can produce a signed statement on request)
- Network flow logs for a bounded window (requires an NDA/approved data request)

If Gridline wants a formal attestation and a redlined SLA clause on deletion windows, we can route that through Legal/Contracts. Happy to join a 30-minute call to walk through the map.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Staff Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
